questions.q: Where is the 'Create deployment pipeline' option found in Power BI?
options: Only inside the tenant admin portal
Right in a workspace's own toolbar, next to options like Create app
Only inside Power BI Desktop, never the service
It must be requested through Microsoft support
questions.explain: Create deployment pipeline sits in the ordinary workspace toolbar, the same one a report author already uses — which is part of why it gets adopted.

questions.q: What does a brand-new deployment pipeline look like before any workspace is assigned?
options: It's unusable until all three workspaces are pre-selected
Three empty, named stage cards — typically Development, Test, and Production — waiting to be connected to real workspaces
A single workspace split into three folders
A blank report with no stages at all
questions.explain: A new pipeline starts as three empty, nameable stages. The structure comes first; assigning actual workspaces to each stage happens afterward.

questions.q: What is each stage of a deployment pipeline actually backed by?
options: A brand-new type of container unique to deployment pipelines
A real, ordinary Power BI workspace, assigned to that stage
A single shared workspace used by all three stages at once
A SharePoint document library
questions.explain: Each stage is a real Power BI workspace. A pipeline is a wrapper connecting three separate workspaces — the same workspace roles and governance from earlier chapters still apply to each one.

questions.q: Why does this lesson say the fact that each stage is a real workspace matters for governance?
options: It doesn't matter — pipelines have entirely separate security rules
Because everything you already know about governing a workspace (roles, tenant settings, sensitivity labels) still applies to each stage individually
Because it means only one person can ever access all three stages
Because workspaces inside a pipeline can't have sensitivity labels
questions.explain: Since each stage is an ordinary workspace, the roles, tenant settings, and sensitivity labels covered in earlier chapters all still apply — a pipeline doesn't replace that governance, it sits on top of it.

questions.q: What kind of control does a stage's own settings menu provide?
options: Only the ability to rename the entire pipeline
Unassigning the workspace from that stage, managing workspace settings, controlling workspace access, and updating a published app
The ability to delete other stages in the pipeline
Changing the color scheme of all reports in the stage
questions.explain: Each stage has its own settings menu covering unassigning its workspace, workspace settings, workspace access, and the app update option — this is where real per-stage governance boundaries get set.
